rounds.text: Hazoor Multi Projects Ltd is currently trading at a significant discount to its intrinsic value, with a margin of safety of 61.8% based on discounted cash flow analysis [E37, E38]. The market has severely mispriced the company's growth trajectory, as the current share price implies a -3.5% earnings growth rate despite the company delivering a 71% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E15, E39]. This disconnect is further highlighted by the stock trading at a price-to-book ratio of 0.54x and an EV/EBITDA of 1.98x, both of which are substantially lower than their respective sector benchmarks [E2, E7, E11, E50]. Institutional confidence is building, evidenced by foreign institutions increasing their holdings from 9.39% to 26.79% since December 2023 [E34]. Furthermore, the company is operating within a sector tailwind and has demonstrated a massive expansion in operating margins, which reached 81% in the most recent quarter [E23, E63, E65]. Conceded: the stock is currently lagging the market with a relative-strength rating of 0, promoter holdings have decreased by 12.23 percentage points, and free cash flow was negative at Rs -282 Cr in March 2026 [E28, E33, E43, E54].

Hazoor Multi Projects Ltd faces significant structural concerns despite its low valuation multiples. The company’s financial health is undermined by a massive free cash flow deficit of Rs -282 Cr [E28] and a concerning increase in borrowings to Rs 478 Cr [E31]. Operational efficiency is deteriorating, evidenced by working capital days ballooning from 304 to 470 days [E55] and contingent liabilities reaching Rs 415 Cr [E53]. Furthermore, the sharp decline in promoter ownership from 25.93% to 13.70% over the last three years signals a lack of long-term commitment from insiders [E33, E54]. Market sentiment remains deeply negative, with the stock sitting near its 52-week low [E5, E40], trading below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E42], and holding a relative-strength rating of zero [E43, E62]. Conceded: [E1, E2, E11, E37] The company does trade at attractive valuation metrics and shows strong recent profit growth, yet these figures are overshadowed by the persistent volatility and poor risk-adjusted returns represented by a Sharpe ratio of -4.67 [E46].

The bear highlights a free cash flow deficit of Rs -282 Cr [E28], but overlooks the fact that operating cash flow was robust at Rs 97 Cr in Mar 2026 with profits fully backed by cash at a 2.26x conversion rate [E26, E27]. Conceded: [E31] Borrowings have indeed risen to Rs 478 Cr [E31], yet short-term liquidity remains comfortable with a current ratio of 2.23x [E30]. While the bear points to ballooning working capital and contingent liabilities [E53, E55], it ignores that operating margins have expanded dramatically to 66% in TTM and hit 81% in Sep 2026 [E22, E23], alongside a massive 71% compounded profit growth [E15]. The declining promoter holding [E33, E54] is heavily offset by foreign institutional accumulation surging to 26.79% [E34] and positive institutional money flow [E36]. Finally, the negative market sentiment and lagging relative-strength [E42, E43] represent precisely the kind of lagging indicator that a turnaround scenario with 100/100 results and accelerating YoY net profit growth of 107% ignores at the investor's peril [E59, E64].

While operating cash flow reached Rs 97 Cr in Mar 2026 [E27], the bull ignores that free cash flow simultaneously plunged to an alarming deficit of Rs -282 Cr [E28] and working capital days bloated from 304 to 470 days [E55]. Conceded: short-term liquidity is marked by a 2.23x current ratio [E30], but total borrowings continued climbing to Rs 478 Cr [E31] alongside massive contingent liabilities of Rs 415 Cr [E53]. The massive margin expansion touted by the bull [E22, E23] is directly undermined by an inconsistent yearly operating-margin trend [E24] and a contracting TTM sales growth rate of -20% [E14]. Conceded: foreign institutions increased holdings to 26.79% [E34], yet promoter ownership has severely deteriorated down to 13.70% after continuous multi-year reductions [E33, E54]. Finally, dismissing lagging price action as mere sentiment [E64] ignores the harsh reality of a relative-strength rating of 0, a miserable Sharpe ratio of -4.67, and a stock price pinned at the absolute floor of its 52-week range [E5, E43, E46].
